thread.title: New iPhone Sales Off to ‘Soft Start,’ Survey Shows - Barron's

title: New iPhone Sales Off to ‘Soft Start,’ Survey Shows - Barron's
text:
New iPhone Sales Off to ‘Soft Start,’ Survey Shows By Nov. 29, 2018 12:25 p.m. ET Order Reprints The new iPhone X. Photograph by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Text size
Canaccord Genuity is joining some of its Wall Street peers and lowering iPhone sales forecasts.
Canaccord analyst T. Michael Walkley reduced his price target to $225 from $250 for Apple shares (AAPL), citing disappointing results from wireless-carrier surveys.
Our North American “surveys indicated soft smartphone and overall iPhone demand,” he wrote on Wednesday. “Our surveys indicated declining sell through share levels from the October launch and disappointing overall sales due in part to soft smartphone demand.”
Apple stock is trading down 1.6% to $178.12 on Thursday.
The analyst said the less-expensive iPhone XR is underperforming versus his previous expectations. He cited the phone’s lack of a high-resolution display and perceived lower build quality as reasons for the shortfall.
The smartphone maker’s $749 iPhone XR went on sale Oct. 26 . The release came after the company put the $999 iPhone XS and the $1,099 iPhone XS Max on the market in September.
“Given the soft start to the latest lineup of iPhones, we are lowering our iPhone estimates and forecast lower year-over-year unit sales in C’19,” Walkley wrote.
He reduced his 2019 iPhone sales estimate to 208 million from 218 million.
Last week, The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple has cut orders in recent weeks for all three newly released iPhone models.
Apple stock has fallen about 19% this month as investors grow increasingly worried about iPhone sales.
Earlier this month, wireless chip maker Qorvo (QRVO) reduced its financial guidance for its third quarter, citing weaker demand for high-end smartphones. And iPhone suppliers Lumentum Holdings (LITE) and Japan Display (6740.Japan) lowered their financial forecasts on Nov. 12.
Despite his lower estimates, Walkley is still bullish on Apple shares for the long term and reaffirmed his Buy rating for the stock.
The analyst’s move came after Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives lowered his price target on Apple on Wednesday before the market open.
